strategy.summary: CART-31 reports two mispricings in cartTotal (src/cart.js). Reading the code: bulkDiscount uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount (report 1 reproduces and is kept as an expected failure). The SAVE5 report doesn't reproduce: goods are already floored at 0 and $4.99 shipping is added, so a $3 cart with SAVE5 costs 4.99. The tests reproduce report 1, pin the report-2 behaviour as a regression test, and check the boundaries on both sides.
inScope: cartTotal bulk discount at, below and above BULK_THRESHOLD (single and multi-line carts)
cartTotal with SAVE5 when the coupon exceeds, equals or is below the goods value
outOfScope: Fixing src/cart.js (the ticket asks for reproduction before a fix)
assumptions: Q1 is unanswered: report 2 is tested as the ticket describes it ($3 single line, SAVE5 → 4.99) and passes on the current code. It is reported as not reproducible, not as a defect.

Expected totals follow the documented rules in src/cart.js: bulk discount of 10% from BULK_THRESHOLD items ("at least this many"), then the coupon, goods floored at 0, plus $4.99 shipping unless the discounted goods reach $50.
openQuestions: Q1: is there another cart shape for the negative-total SAVE5 report, given that the ticket's scenario returns 4.99 today?

risks.description: The off-by-one in the bulk threshold overcharges every 10-item cart
risks.mitigation: TC1/TC2 reproduce it as expected failures, and TC3/TC4 pin both sides of the boundary with passing tests

risks.description: A future fix to the threshold or the coupon floor could break the neighbouring behaviour (no discount at 9 items, coupon still applied on bigger carts)
risks.mitigation: Passing tests for 9 items, 11 items across lines, and SAVE5 on a $20 cart

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart holding exactly 10 items in total (the threshold), on one line or across several, gets the 10% bulk discount: 10 × $10 costs $90.00
A cart below 10 items gets no bulk discount, and one above 10 does (quantities summed across lines)
With SAVE5 the goods never cost less than $0: a $3 cart with SAVE5 costs $4.99 (shipping only)
SAVE5 takes $5 off goods worth more than $5, and an unknown coupon is refused

defects.title: No bulk discount for a cart of exactly 10 items
defects.description: AC1: a cart with exactly BULK_THRESHOLD (10) items should get the 10% bulk discount (10 × $10 → $90.00). bulkDiscount in src/cart.js:22 uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`, which contradicts its own doc ("at least this many"). So cartTotal returns 100. The same thing happens when the 10 items are split across lines (TC2).
defects.evidence: TC1 and TC2 are it.fails and fail as expected: cartTotal([{ price: 10, quantity: 10 }]) returns 100, expected 90.

questions.question: Report 2 (a $3 cart with SAVE5 coming to a negative total) doesn't reproduce in the current src/cart.js. cartTotal already floors the goods at 0 with Math.max(0, …) and adds $4.99 shipping, so it returns 4.99. Should I keep it as a normal passing regression test and tell the team it doesn't reproduce, or do you know of a different cart shape (more lines, other prices) that customers saw?
questions.assumption: I'll test the ticket's exact scenario ($3, one line, SAVE5 → 4.99) as a normal passing regression test, add an edge case where the coupon equals the subtotal, and report that it doesn't reproduce. Only report 1 (the bulk threshold) gets an expected-failure test and a defect.
questions.answer: No preference from the reviewer: decide yourself from the code, record the decision as an assumption and carry on.
